map: B regularizes the dual with mu=min{L,epsilon^2/(2^20 L D_Y^2)} and mu=L for D_Y=0; kappa=L/mu=Theta(Bbar^2). It treats anchor error as a fixed bias conditional on anchor history, uses independent inner averaging and fresh martingale increments, and absorbs error into envelope descent.
B.5 proves fixed U_avg<=C[n+(1+A)(sqrt(n)Bbar+Bbar^4)] and E||grad Phi_{1/(2L)}(c_J)||^2<epsilon^2/200. Markov gives success at least 199/200. There is no logarithm.

C.1-C.4 use projected SVRG under mean-squared operator smoothness and average strong monotonicity, a checked normal-cone residual, and acceleration of a genuine convex dual objective with weighted primal averaging. The compact primal ball is derived from Delta and D_Y.
C.5 prescribes all horizons and aborts on residual failure. U_acc<=C(1+A)(n+n^{3/4}B)ell and success is at least 3/4. No squared-expectation guarantee is claimed for its arbitrary abort output.

proofs.full_local_argument: Write b=max(1,B), X=sqrt(n)b+b^4 and Y=n^{3/4}b. If B<=n^{1/6}, then b<=n^{1/6} because n>=1. Thus b^4<=sqrt(n)b and Y>=sqrt(n)b, so min(X,Y) is between sqrt(n)b and twice that quantity. Lower branch (13) has coefficient sqrt(n)b since sqrt(n)b<=n^{2/3}<=n^{3/4}. U_avg matches because 1+A=O(A). If n^{1/6}<=B<=n^{1/4}, then B>=1 and sqrt(n)B<=B^4<=n^{3/4}B. Hence F is between B^4 and 2B^4. Branch (14) supplies n+A B^4 and U_avg matches. If B>=n^{1/4}, then B>=1 and B^4>=n^{3/4}B, so F=n^{3/4}B. Branch (14) supplies the lower bound. U_acc is O((n+A n^{3/4}B)ell) because n^{3/4}B>=n and A exceeds a positive universal threshold. Separately witnessed minimax lower bounds may be combined by taking their maximum; no common hard instance is needed. IS(L) is contained in AS(L), so T_IS<=T_AS, and both upper witnesses hold under AS(L). This proves the sandwich and windows, including B=0 and n=1.

assumptions: For every x, the average f(x,.) is concave. Individual components need not be concave. Phi is bounded below and Phi(x^0)-inf Phi<=Delta.

IS(L): ||grad f_i(z)-grad f_i(z')||<=L||z-z'|| for every i,z,z'. AS(L): n^{-1}sum_i||grad f_i(z)-grad f_i(z')||^2<=L^2||z-z'||^2 for every z,z'. IS implies AS. AS, not smoothness of the average alone, is the upper class.

One query chooses any i in [n] and any feasible (x,y) and returns exact (f_i,grad_x f_i,grad_y f_i). Choices may be adaptive or repeated; arbitrary query norms, private randomness, full transcript dependence and unqueried outputs are allowed. Computation and memory are unrestricted. Projection onto known Y is free. No free initial dual maximizer, prox or Moreau-gradient Oracle, or uniform component affine-gradient bound is supplied.
L is the same class constant used in A,B and the Moreau parameter. Strong concavity is not required.
statement.conclusion: There exist universal A_*,c,C>0 such that for A>=A_*: c[n+A F(n,B)]<=T_IS<=T_AS<=C[n+A F(n,B)]ell. More precisely, for either class: Theta(n+A sqrt(n)Bbar) for 0<=B<=n^{1/6}; Theta(n+A B^4) for n^{1/6}<=B<=n^{1/4}; and lower c(n+A n^{3/4}B), upper C(n+A n^{3/4}B)ell for B>=n^{1/4}. Only the last upper bound hides a logarithm. Retain additive n and Bbar, including D_Y=0.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Euclidean x in R^{d_x}, z=(x,y), and known nonempty compact convex Y subset R^{d_y} with diam(Y)<=D_Y. Components are differentiable on a neighborhood of R^{d_x} x Y; smoothness and queries are restricted to that product. f=n^{-1}sum_i f_i; Phi(x)=max_Y f(x,y). Define A=L Delta/epsilon^2, B=L D_Y/epsilon, Bbar=max{1,B}, F(n,B)=min{sqrt(n)Bbar+Bbar^4,n^{3/4}Bbar}, ell=log(2+n+A+B). Phi_{1/(2L)}(c)=min_x{Phi(x)+L||x-c||^2}; p(c) is its unique minimizer. T_IS,T_AS are the least worst-case fixed budgets achieving P(||grad Phi_{1/(2L)}(xhat)||<=epsilon)>=2/3 in the respective classes.
statement.parameter_domains: n integer >=1; L,Delta,epsilon>0; D_Y>=0; A>=a universal A_*. Worst case includes admissible finite dimensions; no fixed-low-dimension guarantee is asserted.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: There exist universal constants such that the claim holds for every admissible parameter tuple. Upper witnesses work on every admissible instance, known domain and finite dimension. Lower bounds cover every measurable randomized adaptive algorithm: each insufficient-budget algorithm fails the 2/3 criterion on some fixed admissible finite-dimensional instance and known domain, which may be a Euclidean ball. This is existential hard-domain hardness, not hardness for every shape of a given diameter. Different lower terms may use different families, fixed independently of the private seed.
